result.note: Tests the Supreme Court's February 2026 order on West Bengal's SIR: the extension, the nature of an SIR and the limits on micro-observers.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal:
items: In February 2026, the Supreme Court extended the deadline for West Bengal's SIR by one week beyond February 14.
Unlike routine reviews of the rolls, an SIR requires every voter to be re-verified.
The micro-observers monitoring the process are employees of the West Bengal government.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the story describes micro-observers as Central Government employees who monitor and report on the SIR process. The Court granted the one-week extension on 9 February 2026 while warning it would not create impediments to the Election Commission's exercise.
questions.source: On Monday, the Supreme Court extended West Bengal’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) deadline by one week beyond February 14, while warning that the Court will not create any impediments to the SIR.

questions.prompt: Under the Supreme Court's February 2026 order on West Bengal's Special Intensive Revision, who holds the final decision on deleting voters from the rolls?
questions.explain: The Court ruled that micro-observers may assist but cannot adjudicate, so final decisions on deletions stay with Electoral Registration Officers. This addressed Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee's fear of shadow decision-making by outside observers.
questions.source: Final decisions on voter deletions stay with Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), addressing Banerjee’s fear of shadow decision-making by outside observers.
